title: A meadow splits the meal
hook: Follow the arrows through a small food web.

doesNotKnow: Food-web arrows point from a food source to its consumer.

misconception: A food-web arrow points from predator to prey.
objective: Read direct feeding links and energy-flow direction in a specified food web.

claims.text: Question, diagram and explanation: In this simplified food web, arrows point from food to eater. Which organisms receive energy directly from Grass? The highlighted arrows point from Grass to Rabbit and Mouse. These arrows represent feeding links in this stipulated web; real food webs have additional species and links.
claims.source: Stipulated teaching model; arrow convention: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/46-1-ecology-of-ecosystems

claims.text: This web is a selected hypothetical model, not a complete or universally observed food web.
Recall: An arrow goes from Grass to Rabbit in a food web. What does the arrow indicate? The arrow points from the food source toward the consumer.

recall.question: An arrow goes from Grass to Rabbit in a food web. What does the arrow indicate?
recall.why: The arrow points from the food source toward the consumer.
